programme.desc: Spòrs beò agus geàrr-chunntasan an latha bho Glaschu 2026. Air a lìbhrigeadh le Derek ‘Pluto’ Moireach agus sgioba aithris BBC ALBA. Live sporting action and highlights from Glasgow 2026. Presented by Derek ‘Pluto’ Murray and BBC ALBA’s commentary team.

programme.title: Rudan Beaga Bòidheach/Life’s Little Things
programme.desc: Tha Niamh NicFhionghain a’ coinneachadh daoine òga eile gus rudan beaga fheuchainn a tha a’ toirt toileachas dhaibh. Bho Iòga air mullach cnoc, a bhith a’ sgrìobhadh bàrdachd, gu furachas, dòigh-beatha a’ bhana-campachaidh no a bhith a’ cluich camanachd – tha tòrr ann air an urrainn dhut a bhith taingeil an uair a tha thu air a’ bhlàr a-muigh. Skye digital creator Niamh Mackinnon meets other young people to try out the different little activities that spark joy for them. From hilltop yoga, writing poems, mindfulness, campervan life to playing shinty - there’s so much to appreciate when you just get out there. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Tha Somhairle agus athair a’ cur an dàimh a th’aca gu deuchainn air Ìle agus Diùra, le aon teanta bheag, dà stòbha campachaidh agus aon bhaidhsagal airson dithis! Somhairle and his dad test the limits of their relationship on Islay and Jura - equipped with one small tent, two camping stoves and a bicycle made for two!

programme.title: Binneas - Na Trads
programme.desc: Seata cuirme le Sgoil Chiùil na Gàidhealtachd agus Hadhirgaan, clàraichte beò aig Duaisean nan Trads, 2025. A’ gabhail a-steach Fisherrow Set agus Netherbow Set. Concert set performed by Sgoil Chiùil na Gàidhealtachd and Hadhirgaan, recorded live at the Trad Awards, 2025. Featured tracks include Fisherrow Set and Netherbow Set.

programme.title: Slighe Naoimh Cuithbeirt/St Cuthbert's Way
programme.desc: Iagan MacNèill a’leantail Slighe Naoimh Chuithbeirt a Monadh Weetwood gu Lindisfarne. Iagan MacNeil explores the St Cuthbert’s Way, from Weetwood Moor to Lindisfarne.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean à Coats ann am Pàislig, air a lìbhrigeadh le Iain MacFhionghain. Am measg na seinneadairean bidh Emma NicLeòid, Hamish Scott agus Rona NicLeòid le Donnchadh MacLeòid. Cuideachd, an còisir Soisgeul fo stiùir Gareth Fuller. Bidh Maighstir Seumas MacNèill a’ meòrachadh air cuspair creideimh le leughadh agus smuain, dàn is seallaidhean spioradail ann an companachd Dòmhnall Eachann Meek ann an Tiriodh agus bidh Chloe Steele a’ toirt dhuinn seirm adhraidh air a’ phìob à Manachainn nan Lios. Iain MacKinnon presents a mix of hymns, psalms and readings from Coats in Paisley. Amongst the singers performing are Emma MacLeod, Hamish Scott, and Rona MacLeod with Duncan MacLeod. Also appearing is the choir Soisgeul, conducted by Gareth Fuller. Father James MacNeil reflects on his beliefs with a selected reading and thought, spiritual poetry and landscapes in the company of Donald E Meek in Tiree and Chloe Steele performs a tune of worship on the pipes from Beauly Priory. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: DR NZ
programme.desc: Dr Euan MacDonald moves to Rotorua in New Zealand to work in the city’s hospital. An Dr. Euan Dòmhnallach a' dol gu Sealann Nuadh, a dh' obair san ospadal ann an Rotorua.

programme.title: Geamaichean a' Cho-fhlaitheis Glaschu 2026/Commonwealth Games Glasgow 2026
programme.desc: Craoladh beò bho Cuirm Crìochnachaidh Geamaichean a’ Cho-fhlaitheis ann an Glaschu. Live coverage of the closing ceremony at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. This programme will be available on BBC ALBA iPlayer only from 2200.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Tha Fiona NicChoinnich is Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ toirt thugainn prògram bhon latha mu dheireadh de Belladrum 2026. Chuir an fhèis fàilte air sàr-luchd-ciùil chun na Gàidhealtachd, agus anns a’ phrògram seo, tha taisbeanaidhean beothail bho James, Razorlight, Skerryvore, Sigala agus Kezia Gill. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald present coverage from the final day of Belladrum 2026. The festival welcomes an incredible musical line-up to the Scottish Highlands, and this programme features performances from James, Razorlight, Skerryvore, Sigala and Kezia Gill.

programme.title: The Fairy-Tale Castles of King Ludwig II with Dan Cruickshank
programme.desc: Ludwig II of Bavaria, more commonly known by his nicknames the Swan King or the Dream King, is a legendary figure - the handsome boy-king, loved by his people, betrayed by his cabinet and found dead in tragic and mysterious circumstances. He spent his life in pursuit of the ideal of beauty, which found expression in three of the most extraordinary, ornate architectural schemes imaginable - the castle of Neuschwanstein and the palaces of Linderhof and Herrenchiemsee. Today, these three buildings are among Germany's biggest tourist attractions. In this documentary, Dan Cruickshank explores the rich aesthetic of Ludwig II - from the mock-medievalism of Neuschwanstein, the iconic fairy-tale castle that became the inspiration for the one in Walt Disney's Sleeping Beauty, to the rich, baroque splendour of Herrenchiemsee, Ludwig's answer to Versailles. Dan argues that Ludwig's castles are more than flamboyant kitsch and are, in fact, the key to unravelling the eternal enigma of Ludwig II.

programme.title: A Year in the Wild
programme.desc: The harsh beauty and surprising wildlife of Scotland's Cairngorms National Park through the eyes of the people who know it best. The Cairngorms is Britain's largest and wildest National Park. A land of Arctic extremes in the heart of the Scottish highlands. Its granite mountains and ancient pine forests are home to some of our rarest and most spectacular animals, including golden eagles, ptarmigan, capercaillie, red deer and crested tits. This lyrical and thought-provoking film reveals the inner secrets of this wild landscape over a year through the eyes of individuals who know and love the Cairngorms: a mountain guide, an artist, a salmon ghillie, a gamekeeper and a nature writer.

programme.title: BBC Proms
programme.desc: Rising star Sueye Park dazzles with her Proms debut, playing the Sibelius Violin Concerto. Joined by John Storgårds and the BBC Philharmonic Orchestra, a wildly virtuosic exploration of the Nordic landscape clearly demonstrates how Park won the prestigious 13th International Jean Sibelius Violin Competition last year. The programme continues with two celebrated violinists from Proms past: Liya Petrova playing the much-loved Lark Ascending and Nicola Benedetti performing the playful, lyrical second movement of Wynton Marsalis’s Fiddle Dance Suite. Katie Derham presents a look at some of the great performances on the violin that have graced the Royal Albert Hall stage.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Actor Bill Paterson looks back on one of the earliest roles of his career, in the 1974 boundary-breaking television adaptation of John McGrath's play The Cheviot, the Stag and the Black, Black Oil. It featured outdoor historical re-enactments of the notorious Highland Clearances intercut with scenes from a live performance of the play. Bill's involvement with the production began when he was a young member of left-wing theatre company 7:84 - so named to reflect their claim that seven per cent of the population owned 84 per cent of the UK's wealth. It saw Bill originally playing not one but two roles, as Glasgow property speculator McChuckemup and the oilman known as Texas Bill.

programme.title: Play for Today
programme.desc: The 1974 TV adaptation of John McGrath's iconic 7:84 play about the exploitation of the Scottish people through history, from the aftermath of Culloden to the oil boom.

programme.title: Ex-S
programme.desc: Robert Dawson Scott presents an in-depth look at fortunes of the 7:84 Theatre Company, founded by John McGrath in the late 1960s. Includes excerpts from stage performances and archive interviews.

programme.title: Munro: Mountain Man
programme.desc: Little more than 100 years ago, Scottish mountains standing at more than 3,000 feet were virtually unknown. Today they are familiar terrain to many thousands of climbers, thanks to Victorian adventurer Hugh Munro's determination to list the high peaks which now define the highlands and islands of Scotland. This documentary tells the story of the magnificent peaks that bear his name and the people who have been possessed by them. The birth of this obsession - now known as Munrobagging - is a twisting tale of intrigue, which presenter Nicholas Crane unravels high on the ridges and pinnacles of some of Scotland's most spectacular mountains.

programme.title: AI Decoded
programme.desc: AI Decoded asks whether the AI revolution is delivering on its promises. Companies and organisations are spending vast sums on artificial intelligence after being promised AI will transform productivity, improve efficiency and unlock entirely new ways of working. Yet a growing number of investors and analysts are asking a simple question: where's the proof? Research suggests only a small percentage of enterprise AI projects are producing measurable value. Businesses have bought the software, invested in licences and launched pilot projects, but many are still struggling to turn that investment into meaningful results. So is AI failing to live up to expectations? Or are companies simply approaching adoption the wrong way.

programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. This week, BBC Eye talks to Ukrainians civilians abused in Russian-occupied Ukraine and tracks down the prison guards, officials and soldiers likely responsible. And Kurumi Mori explores a question now shaping the future of Japan: as the country relies more on foreign workers, can it embrace greater diversity without losing what it means to be Japanese?

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: For 11 months of the year, the city of La Vega is well off the tourist track. But each February, it bursts into life. Over the course of four weekends, it’s loud, hot and colourful as visitors from all over the world arrive to join in the famous street carnivals. Clive is in the party mood and throws himself into the fun. He stocks up on local sweet treats, meets talented mask makers and prepares outrageous costumes before joining the parade in full costume.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: The Economist's interview with Elon Musk attracted global attention before Musk then described interviewer Zanny Minton Beddoes as a 'traitor to the West'. The interview followed 90 minutes of conversation for The Insider, The Economist's video series. Zanny Minton Beddoes, Editor-in-Chief of The Economist, explains how the interview came about and the reaction after it was published. Huge wildfires in France and Spain have dominated news coverage across Europe, creating difficult and sometimes dangerous conditions for journalists reporting from the scene. Sadiya Chowdhury, correspondent at Sky News, explains her approach, and Mehdi Lebouachera, global director at AFP, gives the backstory to a photograph that appeared on front pages around the world.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: The pilgrims head into Eryri National Park as the pilgrim path leads the group to one of Wales’s most famous natural wonders, Aber Falls. They take a detour to the island of Anglesey, which is rich in pre-Christian history. The pilgrim path then goes right past Yr Wyddfa, or Mount Snowdon, the highest mountain in England and Wales, where the group rise to the challenge and attempt the summit. Along the way, they discuss grief, forgiveness and the overwhelming power of nature.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Blacksmith Kev 'smashes it' with big profits produced from a glass table, and Sarah gets her wires crossed trying to save a lamp stand.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Just down the road from today’s antiques fair in Nottinghamshire is Southwell Minster, a place of worship for more than a thousand years. Inside the minster’s chapter house, Charlie Ross marvels at the Leaves of Southwell, one of the world’s finest examples of 13th-century stone carvings. At Southwell Racecourse, two teams gallop around the stalls looking for bargains. The red team are friends Connor and James, skippered by expert Nick Hall. Lining up against them are couple Ruth and Emma, with Izzie Balmer. The reds almost get the hump when they see two camel figurines, and the blues don’t take a shine to a pair of bonbon dishes. What will the teams end up spending their £300 on? And will it be a photo finish at Caroline Hawley’s auction at another racecourse – Beverley in the East Riding of Yorkshire?

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Television and radio presenter Angellica Bell and her husband, former fellow children’s TV favourite Michael Underwood, team up with Nicki Chapman to find a family home in the Devon countryside. The property-savvy pair might even roll up their sleeves and get mucky, as there are talks of full-scale renovations at a 1930s period property.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In the first of four special episodes, Adam Henson meets a new generation of farmers navigating the challenges and opportunities of producing our food. Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. Adam joins her on the daily rounds to discover the realities of running a traditional hill farm and hears how she is balancing the responsibility of carrying on a family legacy with the need to build a resilient business for the future. Adam also looks back through the show's archives at some of the inspirational young farmers we have met across the UK.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow is at Brodie Castle in the north of Scotland, where the programme kicks off with some Highland dancing. Fiona Bruce meets a Highland Games commentator who has brought along a collection of items, including a weighty shot put, a heavy hammer and a brooch presented by Queen Victoria in 1848. Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet uncovers a brush pot found at the bottom of the sea, while Matthew Haley takes a closer look at a book by Bram Stoker that was discovered in a charity shop. Marc Allum gets to grips with a gigantic painting that once graced the walls of a hotel in Inverness, and jewellery expert Susan Rumfitt is wowed by a beautiful art deco diamond brooch. Gordon Foster challenges Fiona to put three pieces of Scottish designer jewellery in order of value, while Lee Young comes face to face with a three-legged ceramic toad, and Richard Price casts his expert eye over a Rolex GMT-Master with a hefty price tag.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Gabs and Dick uncover evidence that Leonard is hiding something, while floods in India match Bethany’s drawings. Gabs pushes her suspicions into the open.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.desc: The latest news, sport, weather and features from the South West of England.

programme.title: The Impossible
programme.desc: Thailand, Boxing Day 2004. A tsunami devastates the coast and separates members of a holidaying family of five. Their traumatic experiences give a glimpse of the horrors faced in the aftermath by locals and visitors alike.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. Adam joins her on the daily rounds to discover the realities of running a traditional hill farm and hears how she is balancing the responsibility of carrying on a family legacy with the need to build a resilient business for the future. Adam also looks back through the show's archives at some of the inspirational young farmers we have met across the UK.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow is at Brodie Castle in the north of Scotland, where the programme kicks off with some Highland dancing. Fiona Bruce meets a Highland Games commentator who has brought along a collection of items, including a weighty shot put, a heavy hammer and a brooch presented by Queen Victoria in 1848. Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet uncovers a brush pot found at the bottom of the sea, while Matthew Haley takes a closer look at a book by Bram Stoker that was discovered in a charity shop. Marc Allum gets to grips with a gigantic painting that once graced the walls of a hotel in Inverness, and jewellery expert Susan Rumfitt is wowed by a beautiful art deco diamond brooch. Gordon Foster challenges Fiona to put three pieces of Scottish designer jewellery in order of value, while Lee Young comes face to face with a three-legged ceramic toad, and Richard Price casts his expert eye over a Rolex GMT-Master with a hefty price tag.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Just down the road from today’s antiques fair in Nottinghamshire is Southwell Minster, a place of worship for more than a thousand years. Inside the minster’s chapter house, Charlie Ross marvels at the Leaves of Southwell, one of the world’s finest examples of 13th-century stone carvings. At Southwell Racecourse, two teams gallop around the stalls looking for bargains. The red team are friends Connor and James, skippered by expert Nick Hall. Lining up against them are couple Ruth and Emma, with Izzie Balmer. The reds almost get the hump when they see two camel figurines, and the blues don’t take a shine to a pair of bonbon dishes. What will the teams end up spending their £300 on? And will it be a photo finish at Caroline Hawley’s auction at another racecourse – Beverley in the East Riding of Yorkshire?

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In the first of four special episodes, Adam Henson meets a new generation of farmers navigating the challenges and opportunities of producing our food. Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow is at Brodie Castle in the north of Scotland, where the programme kicks off with some Highland dancing. Fiona Bruce meets a Highland Games commentator who has brought along a collection of items, including a weighty shot put, a heavy hammer and a brooch presented by Queen Victoria in 1848. Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet uncovers a brush pot found at the bottom of the sea, while Matthew Haley takes a closer look at a book by Bram Stoker that was discovered in a charity shop. Marc Allum gets to grips with a gigantic painting that once graced the walls of a hotel in Inverness, and jewellery expert Susan Rumfitt is wowed by a beautiful art deco diamond brooch. programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: The pilgrims head into Eryri National Park as the pilgrim path leads the group to one of Wales’s most famous natural wonders, Aber Falls. They take a detour to the island of Anglesey, which is rich in pre-Christian history. The pilgrim path then goes right past Yr Wyddfa, or Mount Snowdon, the highest mountain in England and Wales, where the group rise to the challenge and attempt the summit. Along the way, they discuss grief, forgiveness and the overwhelming power of nature.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Blacksmith Kev 'smashes it' with big profits produced from a glass table, and Sarah gets her wires crossed trying to save a lamp stand.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Just down the road from today’s antiques fair in Nottinghamshire is Southwell Minster, a place of worship for more than a thousand years. Inside the minster’s chapter house, Charlie Ross marvels at the Leaves of Southwell, one of the world’s finest examples of 13th-century stone carvings. At Southwell Racecourse, two teams gallop around the stalls looking for bargains. The red team are friends Connor and James, skippered by expert Nick Hall. Lining up against them are couple Ruth and Emma, with Izzie Balmer. The reds almost get the hump when they see two camel figurines, and the blues don’t take a shine to a pair of bonbon dishes. What will the teams end up spending their £300 on? And will it be a photo finish at Caroline Hawley’s auction at another racecourse – Beverley in the East Riding of Yorkshire?

Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. Adam joins her on the daily rounds to discover the realities of running a traditional hill farm and hears how she is balancing the responsibility of carrying on a family legacy with the need to build a resilient business for the future. Adam also looks back through the show's archives at some of the inspirational young farmers we have met across the UK.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow is at Brodie Castle in the north of Scotland, where the programme kicks off with some Highland dancing. Fiona Bruce meets a Highland Games commentator who has brought along a collection of items, including a weighty shot put, a heavy hammer and a brooch presented by Queen Victoria in 1848. Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet uncovers a brush pot found at the bottom of the sea, while Matthew Haley takes a closer look at a book by Bram Stoker that was discovered in a charity shop. Marc Allum gets to grips with a gigantic painting that once graced the walls of a hotel in Inverness, and jewellery expert Susan Rumfitt is wowed by a beautiful art deco diamond brooch. Gordon Foster challenges Fiona to put three pieces of Scottish designer jewellery in order of value, while Lee Young comes face to face with a three-legged ceramic toad, and Richard Price casts his expert eye over a Rolex GMT-Master with a hefty price tag.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Gabs and Dick uncover evidence that Leonard is hiding something, while floods in India match Bethany’s drawings. Gabs pushes her suspicions into the open.

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection
programme.desc: Prayer and Reflection from the Sikh gurdwara in Roath, Cardiff. The service is a communal worship in Punjabi, with prayers, musical renditions of scripture and other activities.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: The pilgrims head into Eryri National Park as the pilgrim path leads the group to one of Wales’s most famous natural wonders, Aber Falls. They take a detour to the island of Anglesey, which is rich in pre-Christian history. The pilgrim path then goes right past Yr Wyddfa, or Mount Snowdon, the highest mountain in England and Wales, where the group rise to the challenge and attempt the summit. Along the way, they discuss grief, forgiveness and the overwhelming power of nature.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Blacksmith Kev 'smashes it' with big profits produced from a glass table, and Sarah gets her wires crossed trying to save a lamp stand.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Just down the road from today’s antiques fair in Nottinghamshire is Southwell Minster, a place of worship for more than a thousand years. Inside the minster’s chapter house, Charlie Ross marvels at the Leaves of Southwell, one of the world’s finest examples of 13th-century stone carvings. At Southwell Racecourse, two teams gallop around the stalls looking for bargains. The red team are friends Connor and James, skippered by expert Nick Hall. Lining up against them are couple Ruth and Emma, with Izzie Balmer. The reds almost get the hump when they see two camel figurines, and the blues don’t take a shine to a pair of bonbon dishes. What will the teams end up spending their £300 on? And will it be a photo finish at Caroline Hawley’s auction at another racecourse – Beverley in the East Riding of Yorkshire?

programme.desc: Puss in Boots gets his own animated adventure film in this Shrek spin-off. Puss teams up with a fellow thieving feline and his old friend Humpty Dumpty to embark on an exciting quest. The trio plan to find magic beans in order to steal the goose that lays the golden eggs, but all does not go according to plan. programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: Craig Gordon is famous for his resilience and defiance of strikers, coaches, critics and doctors. He has granted BBC cameras unprecedented access to his life over 12 months as, at the age of 42, he makes one last attempt to reach a World Cup. Along the way, we learn about the miracle saves and comebacks from injuries that should have ended his career and that have allowed him to still compete at the top level for so many years. From a prodigy at Hearts to a record breaker in the English Premier League and an invincible at Celtic, Craig Gordon has had a career like no other, but there is one thing still missing - an appearance at a World Cup. To get there, he will have to overcome opposition on the pitch as well as the limitations of his own body as he battles injuries to keep the dream alive. A fascinating insight into the mind of one of Scotland’s most driven athletes.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: The pilgrims head into Eryri National Park as the pilgrim path leads the group to one of Wales’s most famous natural wonders, Aber Falls. They take a detour to the island of Anglesey, which is rich in pre-Christian history. The pilgrim path then goes right past Yr Wyddfa, or Mount Snowdon, the highest mountain in England and Wales, where the group rise to the challenge and attempt the summit. Along the way, they discuss grief, forgiveness and the overwhelming power of nature.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Just down the road from today’s antiques fair in Nottinghamshire is Southwell Minster, a place of worship for more than a thousand years. Inside the minster’s chapter house, Charlie Ross marvels at the Leaves of Southwell, one of the world’s finest examples of 13th-century stone carvings. At Southwell Racecourse, two teams gallop around the stalls looking for bargains. The red team are friends Connor and James, skippered by expert Nick Hall. Lining up against them are couple Ruth and Emma, with Izzie Balmer. The reds almost get the hump when they see two camel figurines, and the blues don’t take a shine to a pair of bonbon dishes. What will the teams end up spending their £300 on? And will it be a photo finish at Caroline Hawley’s auction at another racecourse – Beverley in the East Riding of Yorkshire?

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In the first of four special episodes, Adam Henson meets a new generation of farmers navigating the challenges and opportunities of producing our food. Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. Adam joins her on the daily rounds to discover the realities of running a traditional hill farm and hears how she is balancing the responsibility of carrying on a family legacy with the need to build a resilient business for the future. Adam also looks back through the show's archives at some of the inspirational young farmers we have met across the UK.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow is at Brodie Castle in the north of Scotland, where the programme kicks off with some Highland dancing. Fiona Bruce meets a Highland Games commentator who has brought along a collection of items, including a weighty shot put, a heavy hammer and a brooch presented by Queen Victoria in 1848. Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet uncovers a brush pot found at the bottom of the sea, while Matthew Haley takes a closer look at a book by Bram Stoker that was discovered in a charity shop. Marc Allum gets to grips with a gigantic painting that once graced the walls of a hotel in Inverness, and jewellery expert Susan Rumfitt is wowed by a beautiful art deco diamond brooch. Gordon Foster challenges Fiona to put three pieces of Scottish designer jewellery in order of value, while Lee Young comes face to face with a three-legged ceramic toad, and Richard Price casts his expert eye over a Rolex GMT-Master with a hefty price tag.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Prayer and Reflection
programme.desc: Prayer and Reflection from the Sikh gurdwara in Roath, Cardiff. The service is a communal worship in Punjabi, with prayers, musical renditions of scripture and other activities.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc: The pilgrims head into Eryri National Park as the pilgrim path leads the group to one of Wales’s most famous natural wonders, Aber Falls. They take a detour to the island of Anglesey, which is rich in pre-Christian history. The pilgrim path then goes right past Yr Wyddfa, or Mount Snowdon, the highest mountain in England and Wales, where the group rise to the challenge and attempt the summit. Along the way, they discuss grief, forgiveness and the overwhelming power of nature.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Blacksmith Kev 'smashes it' with big profits produced from a glass table, and Sarah gets her wires crossed trying to save a lamp stand.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Just down the road from today’s antiques fair in Nottinghamshire is Southwell Minster, a place of worship for more than a thousand years. Inside the minster’s chapter house, Charlie Ross marvels at the Leaves of Southwell, one of the world’s finest examples of 13th-century stone carvings. At Southwell Racecourse, two teams gallop around the stalls looking for bargains. The red team are friends Connor and James, skippered by expert Nick Hall. Lining up against them are couple Ruth and Emma, with Izzie Balmer. The reds almost get the hump when they see two camel figurines, and the blues don’t take a shine to a pair of bonbon dishes. What will the teams end up spending their £300 on? And will it be a photo finish at Caroline Hawley’s auction at another racecourse – Beverley in the East Riding of Yorkshire?

The trio plan to find magic beans in order to steal the goose that lays the golden eggs, but all does not go according to plan. Featuring the voices of Antonio Banderas (Puss), Salma Hayek (Kitty Softpaws), Zach Galifianakis (Humpty Alexander Dumpty), Billy Bob Thornton (Jack), Amy Sedaris (Jill), Constance Marie (Imelda), Guillermo Del Toro (Moustache Man/Commandante) and Mike Mitchell (Andy Beanstalk).

programme.title: Celebrity Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Television and radio presenter Angellica Bell and her husband, former fellow children’s TV favourite Michael Underwood, team up with Nicki Chapman to find a family home in the Devon countryside. The property-savvy pair might even roll up their sleeves and get mucky, as there are talks of full-scale renovations at a 1930s period property.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In the first of four special episodes, Adam Henson meets a new generation of farmers navigating the challenges and opportunities of producing our food. Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. Travelling to Bala in Gwynedd, north Wales, he meets 23-year-old sheep and cattle farmer Erin McNaught. A fourth-generation farmer, Erin manages around 250 acres across three sites in partnership with her grandfather. Adam joins her on the daily rounds to discover the realities of running a traditional hill farm and hears how she is balancing the responsibility of carrying on a family legacy with the need to build a resilient business for the future. Adam also looks back through the show's archives at some of the inspirational young farmers we have met across the UK.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow is at Brodie Castle in the north of Scotland, where the programme kicks off with some Highland dancing. Fiona Bruce meets a Highland Games commentator who has brought along a collection of items, including a weighty shot put, a heavy hammer and a brooch presented by Queen Victoria in 1848. Ceramics expert Serhat Ahmet uncovers a brush pot found at the bottom of the sea, while Matthew Haley takes a closer look at a book by Bram Stoker that was discovered in a charity shop. Marc Allum gets to grips with a gigantic painting that once graced the walls of a hotel in Inverness, and jewellery expert Susan Rumfitt is wowed by a beautiful art deco diamond brooch. Gordon Foster challenges Fiona to put three pieces of Scottish designer jewellery in order of value, while Lee Young comes face to face with a three-legged ceramic toad, and Richard Price casts his expert eye over a Rolex GMT-Master with a hefty price tag.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: Gabs and Dick uncover evidence that Leonard is hiding something, while floods in India match Bethany’s drawings. Gabs pushes her suspicions into the open.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: In the first of four special episodes, Adam Henson meets a new generation of farmers navigating the challenges and opportunities of producing our food. Along the way, Adam gets a glimpse into their daily lives, exploring how they are facing the growing uncertainty in the industry and seeing what innovations they have embraced to secure the future of their farms. programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Antiques Roadshow is at Brodie Castle in the north of Scotland, where the programme kicks off with some Highland dancing. Fiona Bruce meets a Highland Games commentator who has brought along a collection of items, including a weighty shot put, a heavy hammer and a brooch presented by Queen Victoria in 1848. Marc Allum gets to grips with a gigantic painting that once graced the walls of a hotel in Inverness, and jewellery expert Susan Rumfitt is wowed by a beautiful art deco diamond brooch. Gordon Foster challenges Fiona to put three pieces of Scottish designer jewellery in order of value, while Lee Young comes face to face with a three-legged ceramic toad, and Richard Price casts his expert eye over a Rolex GMT-Master with a hefty price tag.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are?
programme.desc: Harriet Walter delves into her family history, discovering ancestors who are just as colourful as some of fictional characters she has played on stage and screen. In a journey that takes her from Whitehall to Italy to Australia, she follows in the footsteps of her ancestors, including her flamboyant Italian great-great-grandfather Girolamo Carindini, an Italian aristocrat who fled into exile and settled in Tasmania. Here, he married Australia’s first opera diva. But drama and trouble followed Girolamo as he made as many headlines for his appearances in the debtor’s court as he did for his theatrical performances.

programme.title: My Epic Camel Adventure with Gordon Buchanan
programme.desc: Gordon Buchanan takes an epic journey across the Gobi Desert on one of the world’s most iconic, yet least understood, animals – camels. Starting in the west of Mongolia, Gordeon crosses blistering sand dunes, endless rocky plains and the treacherous Bumbat Mountain, with only his camels for company. If he is to succeed, he must befriend the camels, learn as much as he can about them, and try to win their trust and respect. Without that, the journey and his survival are in question. Naming camels isn’t something that nomads would do, but as his relationship with them strengthens, he decides to name them Squeaks and Chewy. They are lucky enough to meet some of the other inhabitants of this seemingly desolate landscape, such as wolves, saiga antelopes and yaks. But will he be lucky enough to catch sight of the most endangered bear on the planet – the Gobi Bear? Spending time with different nomads also gives Gordon time to reflect on the appeal of the traditional nomadic way of life, and his own modern existence. Ultimately, he discovers how camels have evolved in the most unusual ways to survive and prosper in one of the most hostile environments on the planet.

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: The Special Operations Response Team are called to the scene of a mountain bike accident in a hilly patch of East Ayrshire woodland. The patient’s bike seat has broken, causing him a painful and potentially dangerous injury. SORT crewmates Pam and Rob must now figure out how to move the patient across difficult ground and into a waiting ambulance. Fortunately, they have their Wolverine all-terrain vehicle to hand. Based in a community of around 10,000 people, Buckie teammates Vicki and Elaine often encounter friends and acquaintances on their ambulance shifts. They treat Isabella, who is struggling with breathing difficulties caused by her COPD, and old school bus driver George, who is displaying the signs of a stroke.

programme.title: Still Game
programme.desc: Sitcom featuring Jack and Victor, two irrepressible pensioners first seen in the comedy series Chewin' the Fat, along with their dependable pals Winston and Tam, fresh out of Craiglang and taking on the world. Yankee happy pills are proving more of a temptation to Jack and Victor after they bump into their old pal Stuart.

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Spoof comedy following the first Unified Scottish Police Force. The traffic cops tackle a dodgy driver, the detectives smash a smuggling operation, and the Chief bravely faces up to encountering his ex-wife. We learn more about SPF special ops as a very important dignitary requires a level of protection that's way beyond the call of duty. And PC Jack McLaren steps in to help out using what could only be described as extreme piggy-backing.

programme.title: Cumming to the Cabaret
programme.desc: Alan kicks off the dog benefit, while Michelle's family attends the show. Daphne shares her Icelandic plans with Alan while grappling with how to break the news to Darren.

programme.title: Cumming to the Cabaret
programme.desc: Darren is motivated by Daphne's announcement and decides to share his ideas with Alan. Daphne, Michelle, Cunning and Jake meet up to talk about their future plans. Darren surprises Daphne with a thoughtful gift during her last performance.

programme.title: TUNE
programme.desc: Addressing the lack of nightlife for young people in the area, Ullapool native Sigi and his friend Jemima take on the challenge of creating Scotland’s most remote club night. Capturing the action as their electronic music night baile/baile is brought to life, Sigi shares his experience of growing up in this remote part of the county and highlights how important music and community are. From immersion in trad and folk at a young age, to the influence of Martyn Bennett and discovering dance music at Rockness Festival, Sigi shares the journey which brought him home to Ullapool to start a club night for the next generation.

programme.desc: Life is hard, so Callum and Jordan, two emotionally unassembled young lads from Northern Ireland, start the Funboys’ Fun Club: a playgroup for childish young men to engage in wholesome mucking about. But when a juice party goes awry, Callum’s ultra-religious fiancée Morgan kicks them out, and the Funboys must search for a new HQ. When they come across Marty, a catatonically depressed 60-year-old, can they bring joy back to his life and prove that fun won't necessarily lead to an eternity spent in raging hellfire?

programme.title: Zara McDermott
programme.desc: This episode tells the story of Gaia going missing from her aunt’s house just before sunset on a November evening in 2017. Just before she leaves, she makes a last-minute call to her identical twin sister, Maya, then she runs. She’s alone without a coat, phone or medication for her epilepsy and in a state of high distress. After making several emergency calls to police, Gaia’s family believe that a widespread search for her is underway. Days later, after hundreds of volunteers have joined the search, Gaia’s body is found deep in undergrowth on Dancing Ledge. She had died of hypothermia. Zara McDermott wants answers; what or who had she been running from? And could the man that Gaia had briefly been seeing have anything to do with her disappearance?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The A to Z of TV Gardening
programme.desc: Carol Kirkwood takes an alphabetical journey through the world of gardening, getting inspiration and advice from some of the BBC's most popular garden presenters and programmes. In this episode, she is exploring subjects that all begin with the letter I.

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: Christine Walkden floats over the landlocked Midlands county of Staffordshire. At Biddulph Grange she takes to the water to help remove some unwelcome guests and meets Helen, the 'heart of the garden'. At Shugborough Hall she rallies the troops for a spot of tree hugging and we discover how the area's proud industrial heritage shaped the county's landscape.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.desc: Derek reflects on his favourite mountain walks like Mynydd Sygun in Eryi National Park, the Black Mountains in the east of Bannau Brycheiniog and Table Mountain in Powys.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Gardening is all about looking ahead, and in that spirit, the Beechgrove Garden team are planning for winter. Ruth Vichos demonstrates how to cultivate and multiply snowdrops, and Calum Clunie collects seeds from this year’s lupins to sow for future colour. Calum also gets his feet wet as he looks at what you should be doing about pond maintenance right now. Ruth is in her strawberry bed discussing how you should be getting the most from your crop, and she also profiles some the country’s favourite garden plants in her competition plot. There is a visit to a fabulous garden in Orkney, along with all the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt delves into the Saturday Kitchen archives to bring you some delicious recipes from years gone by. Sabrina Ghayour prepares halloumi fattah and simple spiced flatbreads. Ravinder Bhogal serves up a sharing starter with cured sea bream, sweet melon and a jalapeno and lime dressing. Theo Randall puts tuna centre stage with seared tuna steak and a light potato, green bean and pea salad, finished with a punch anchovy and rosemary dressing. Jaega Wise goes on a trip around the world with her top picks of global beers, while Marianne Lumb presents her white peach and ruby chocolate crostata. Finally, Ellie Taylor tucks into either her food heaven, ricotta and burrata cannelloni, or her food hell, hay-smoked venison. Meanwhile, Rick Stein heads to Scotland for a taste of their unique garlic, and the Hairy Bikers get milking on a sheep farm in Sardinia.

programme.title: Indian Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Food writer and chef Anjum Anand is on a mission to show how simple it is to cook healthy Indian meals. In this episode, she attempts to put some light dishes on the menu at a luxury hotel and spa. Anjum demonstrates how to make stuffed dhosas, a type of pancake; avial, a mixed vegetable dish accompanied by a slightly sweet Bengal gram lentil curry; and shrikand, a yoghurt-based dessert made with saffron. An Ayurvedic expert reveals how the ingredients of Indian food have medicinal properties.

programme.title: Indian Food Made Easy
programme.desc: Anjum Anand heads for an Essex fire station to show Paul Pemberton and the blue watch how to cook aubergine in yoghurt, a lamb curry with squat green chillies and homemade naan.

programme.title: Loch Ness
programme.desc: An American scientist meets hostility from loch locals as he tries to prove the existence of the Loch Ness monster.

programme.desc: Coverage of The Hundred 100-ball cricket tournament.

programme.desc: Coverage of The Hundred 100-ball cricket tournament.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: The brilliant Nabil Abdulrashid introduces Jake Lambert and Rachel Fairburn to the stage.

programme.title: Shakespeare in Love
programme.desc: William Shakespeare hasn't written a hit in years, and theatre owner Henslowe is counting on Shakespeare's promised comedy, Romeo and Ethel, the Pirate's Daughter, to keep his wolfish creditors from the door. At the casting session, Will hears his lines spoken with great feeling by an unknown young actor, and his curiosity is fired. Soon he discovers the secret of the talented young actor and rediscovers his muse. As Shakespeare falls in love with an unattainable noblewoman, the farcical comedy transforms into the timeless tragedy that is Romeo and Juliet.

programme.title: Golf: Women's Open
programme.desc: Highlights from the final day of the Women’s Open at Royal Lytham & St Annes. England’s Georgia Hall secured a famous victory when the championship was last played on the Lancashire links in 2018. South Korea’s Haeran Ryu begins the week going for a third consecutive major victory, while American world number one Nelly Korda is also looking to make it three major wins this season. Japan’s Miyu Yamashita is the defending champion following an impressive victory at Royal Porthcawl in 2025.

programme.title: Ann Droid
programme.desc: Linda encourages Sue to join Tom and Eileen on a trip to the seaside to scatter ashes. To cheer themselves up, they decide to go to a funfair, where a fortune teller leaves Sue hoping for a sign from Dave and a promise to try new things, starting with a rollercoaster ride. Meanwhile, Michael’s efforts to be a rock star and impress everyone at an open-mic night are totally ruined thanks to Linda.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: The final stop on Anita’s east coast road trip is the mysterious Orford Ness in Suffolk. Once a top-secret military testing facility, this ten-mile shingle spit is now one of Britain's most important protected coastal landscapes, where former military buildings provide nesting sites for seabirds. Anita explores the abandoned military complex to uncover Orford Ness's secretive past and discovers how a landscape once shaped by weapons testing has been reclaimed by wildlife. She also meets an artist inspired to write an album about the area’s fascinating past and its current status as a nature haven. Along the way, Anita looks back through the Countryfile archives at the communities exposed to the sea and how nature can stage a comeback.

Buddy shows her how to make healthy chicken breasts, served with fresh pasta to give them loads of energy, cutting out their own shapes in a cool hack to personalise their pasta and bring it all together with a delicious homemade pesto with added peas – it’s a chicken pea-sto pasta! Worried, she makes a wish to find him, and her wishing wand whisks her and Jake on a wild chase through the park. Finally, back at the bakery, they discover baby Oscar happily playing with Tommy - Amy bought it to cheer him up. Seeing Oscar’s joy, Rafi decides to let him keep Tommy.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Cosima and Big Lizard's solar-powered hoverboards run out of battery at nightfall. Can glowbugs be the answer?

programme.title: Spidey and His Amazing Friends
programme.desc: Rhino turns invisible. Squirrel Girl stops Gobby.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: Two dolphins get stuck in a coastal saltwater lake during low tide.

programme.title: Knee High Spies
programme.desc: Silver Paw plans to turn Scarlett's kit pink, and Jeremy must conquer his fear of heights!

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The Chipmunk accidentally gets hit by a ball during a game of baseball. To make him feel better, the ducklings feed him popcorn. The Chipmunk pretends to be sick to get more and more privileges. Weasy has had enough!

programme.title: Talking Tom Heroes: Suddenly Super
programme.desc: The Heroes meet a mysterious person while on the hunt for a stolen statue.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: It’s recycling day in the attic – and it's also Murphi’s hairdo day! The first idea is a hilarious hairdo pot, the Mini Monsters make a variety of cheese box octopuses, and the Magic Monster Mirror brings a call from Rebecca’s aunt. Finally, the Recycling Express arrives with some buttons that Murphi and Rebecca use to create a brilliant box robot.

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Sienna's dad is from Nigeria, and he has taught her a unique way of making Nigerian jollof rice. Sienna asks her friends to try tasting fresh thyme, which is one of the ingredients in her jollof rice, before they come round for a special Nigerian meal. No one is at all keen on the taste of the thyme, but Sienna is confident that she can change their minds when they try some of her food. Sienna's dad has prepared a colourful Nigerian salad to eat with the rice and they even treat their guests to some Nigerian chin chin to enjoy after the meal. What a lucky bunch!

programme.title: Hamza Loves Animals: Africa
programme.desc: The baby zebras learn that exercise can be lots of fun. Hamza visits the watering hole – a place where lots of wild animals gather. He also joins the elephants on a forest walk.

programme.title: Down on the Farm
programme.desc: Series looking at what happens on farms. Storm visits a farm in Wales to meet some spring lambs, and JB meets young gardeners to see what they grow and plant in their very special school garden. JB also sees how farmers prepare the fields so that new seeds can be sown. Storm shares a Down on the Farm spring poem, and we find out how rhubarb is farmed.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is an adorable talking dog who can't help but cause trouble! His everyday adventures are full of mayhem and mischief. Warning: theme tune guaranteed to stick in your head.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: When a dancing bug lands on Duggee's head, he can't stop dancing. The Squirrels take a close look and see that it's a tiny hillbilly bug with a fiddle. And what's more, he's got a whole band with him - the Hillbilly Bug Band.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: The Octonauts evacuate the creatures living around a reef before a large archway collapses, but one stubborn convict fish refuses to move from her burrow.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Zigzag’s friend, Banjo the koala, doesn’t feel like coming out to play, she calls Vida, who knows just what to do. Vida gets him exercising and healthy enough to play with Zigzag in no time!

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: In Japan, Grandmaster Glitch is at a railway station, wondering where his grimbots have gone. Some excited bleeps further down the platform reveal that they have jumped into the driver's cabin of a bullet train and are happily pressing all the buttons! Glitch shouts at them to stop but it is too late: he quickly jumps onboard as the doors slam shut and the train moves off - leaving the station without its driver. Meanwhile, at the next station, the Go Jetters are excitedly waiting with their tickets to ride the bullet train. The train approaches but doesn't stop, racing past the Go Jetters as Grandmaster Glitch shouts out of the window. The Go Jetters realise the train has been glitched!

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: When a giant beetle steals D.O.R.I.S.'s brain, thinking it's a nut, Cosima and Big Lizard give chase through the forest. Big Lizard uses unique skills to rescue poor D.O.R.I.S.'s superbrain.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Sonny and Yukee are distracted by the amazing musical properties of a pile of old salvaged pots. Unfortunately, Sonny has promised some of the pots to Twinkle, who becomes increasingly impatient while Sonny and Yukee play!

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button discover dental floss and plan an exciting tug-of-war showdown.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and George meet Ellie May in a garden to pick lots of tasty fruit and vegetables. Mr Tumble is running his own shop, and Grandad is his first customer. There are tasty strawberries in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words fruit, cucumber and shop.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Kika is a golden labrador and a guide dog for her owner Dr Amit, who is blind, which means he cannot see. She is trained to use her super sight to help Dr Amit do as many things as he can by himself. Together, they make the best team! Dr Amit is showing his children Abhi and Anoushka how to read braille, a special pattern of clever dots that helps people to read using their fingers. Kika says it’s like a secret code. When Abhi asks if they can visit the library to borrow a braille book for Amit to read to them, Amit checks his braille watch and realises that they’d better hurry. The library is closing soon. First, Kika helps Dr Amit to find Anoushka’s missing coat and Abhi’s lost shoe. Outside the library, there are more clever dots to help Amit find his way. Then, he and Kika follow Abhi and Anoushka to the children’s section. Dr Amit uses more clever dots to find Abhi’s favourite story on the shelf - but then, disaster! The braille pages are missing, and Dr Amit can’t read the story. Kika leaps into action. Can she guide Amit and Abhi to the librarian so they can find the braille printer and get the pages they need before the library closes?

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Sophie and Kassius are looking after their gran’s dog when it escapes. Can they find him before Mr Parks does? He has decided dogs are banned at the Den.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: The doctors visit Fifi and see that she is feeling sad because her pies aren’t up to her usual standard. They take her out to cheer her up - until Zog realises what she really needs.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the Peas discover a more efficient way to explore the valley - by tunnel!

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Steve and Aneeshwar head inside a dark enclosure to give some fruit bats their breakfast. The bats show them how well they can fly around in the dark. Their next encounter is with Wallace the barn owl, who is very chatty and shows Steve and Aneeshwar her wings and talons. They then learn what the bats and barn owl have in common and how they use their special skills in the wild.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the bagpipe-playing Chilli Peppers, melting Kiwi backstage and performing their song We’re Chilli When It’s Hot!.

programme.title: Tish Tash
programme.desc: Bobby and Tish are outside in the garden having a picnic and an ant steals Bobby's cookie! Tish uses her imagination to shrink herself and Bobby down to ant size to continue the pursuit.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Mama and Papa are taking Oona and Baba on a family outing to experience something special - Papa tells them it's a big surprise. Oona and Baba are very excited to see it, but they need to find the perfect spot - which isn't easy. In the end, the amazing surprise makes all of their effort worth it.

programme.title: Love Monster
programme.desc: On the hottest day of the year, Book Cub is worried that she will run out of cups to serve fro-yo in, so Love Monster volunteers to look after her fro-yo van while she goes to get more. But after Bad Idea Puppy encourages him to give out extra fro-yo, he gets carried away and accidentally breaks the fro-yo machine, causing a nasty mess. When Book Cub returns, she is upset, but Love Monster apologises and together with Bad Idea Puppy they clean everything up.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: One is off on a camping adventure, but it can be lonely being the only one. Luckily, Two joins her just in time for a picnic. One puts a picnic blanket down, which is split into two equal parts - one part for One and one part for Two. When they get to the camp ground, they are joined by Three and Four, and together they discover how to split the camping space and baguette into equal parts.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Black joins the Printing Crew. Learn how yellow, cyan, magenta and black work together in printing with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: The Froglets don homemade skis and snowboards to whiz down a mountain of winter duvets.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella and Lift have fun playing with sponges, and so does Tincy the Spider in the Sing Song Forest - just watch out for those soapy bubbles!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: A samba band is coming to play, and everyone is helping to prepare. Stripes is so busy that he has forgotten one thing - to book the band! With no band coming, all seems lost, until Yukee and Stripes realise the Sunhouse already has its own brilliant band!

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children use nets to catch toy fish in a water tray, learning BSL signs for fish, why and bit, then they sing and sign One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Once I Caught a Fish Alive.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Nick is looking at family photographs and creates a Popcast song about being a brother.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The Piris plan a trip to Tippety Top to see the famous southern lights but lose each other in an ice fog. When Nugget thinks she sees a monster, Pancake proves to be an unlikely hero.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: With Pearl entranced by Fifi’s glowing tummy mushrooms, Zog fears the worst when Gadabout attempts to mend Boom's wing himself.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants to blow a bubble just like her dads, but no matter how hard she tries, it won’t work. She makes a wish and creates a huge, magical bubble that floats around the park. As Rafi chases after it, the bubble spreads wonder wherever it goes. But when the bubble finally pops, Rafi is heartbroken. With help from her dads and friends, Rafi realises that bubbles aren’t meant to last forever, and that some of the most special moments are wonderful because they are fleeting.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo must prove Mr Monkeyjocks is special to save him from being chucked out.

programme.title: Nikhil & Jay
programme.desc: Nikhil and Jay start their own rock band. However, Nikhil feels deflated when Jay keeps inviting other people to join the band. Nikhil wants it to be just the two of them.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Umbrella is nervous about meeting up with his pen pal at the Parasol Show, so Sarah and Duck accompany him.

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Children's animation. Join Lola and Charlie, a brother and sister, as they learn about growing up. When Charlie and Lola visit Granny and Grandpa, they always build an extremely special sandcastle on the beach, and they always do it together. This time a little girl and her family are determined to join in, and Lola's not too happy about it.

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: The discovery of a nursery rhyme book in the Toy House inspires Mr Onion to play at being Humpty Dumpty. When Humpty Onion refuses to fall off the wall, all the Toy House friends join in a game to make a comical new ending to the Humpty rhyme.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo plays with a block which is red like MeMo, and BaBa plays with a block that is yellow like BaBa. The friends continue across Planet BeddyByes and see more examples of their special colours: a yellow Tweetie, red and yellow Yummies, and a yellow omelette with red tomatoes. On the Lullaby Lake, reds and yellows mix in the setting sun to create a new, special colour.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read bedtime stories. Upsy Daisy wants to rest in her bed but is disturbed by one character after another. Finally, Upsy Daisy is left alone but discovers that she would much rather play with her friends after all.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Vicky McClure reads a Bedtime Story about a tiger on the hunt for his lost smile.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of potatoes who sing songs in different genres. In this soft lullaby, Moon Baby observes the galaxy from up on the moon before floating back home to his cosy nursery.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona and Baba go to the secret den to shelter from a thunderstorm, where they find Mossy and the Shrew Crew hiding. Mossy admits that he’s afraid of thunder and lightning. Oona encourages Mossy to listen to the music of the storm - the whistling wind, the pattering rain and the booming thunder - and together, they sing the Stormy Song. Maybe thunderstorms aren't so bad after all!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Pando is teaching Bing and Sula how to do little kicks and big kicks with a ball in the garden. Sula does the biggest kick of them all, but Bing kicks the ball the wrong way. As he tries to kick it back to Pando it bounces off the shed, breaking Flop's window! They have to stand statue-still while Flop cleans up the glass.

programme.title: Love Monster
programme.desc: It’s Tidy Up Day, so everyone in Fluffytown is tidying things. Love Monster helps Book Cub to clean up the forest, and as he does so finds several items that would make great souvenirs. These include a bunny-shaped rock, a cloud-shaped leaf and a heart-shaped stone. But he doesn't notice that each time he take a souvenir, it disturbs a forest creature that was using it. Once he finally realises this, he and Book Cub work together to put all of the treasures back in their rightful places.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button use kitchen foil to create and launch an out-of-this-world spaceship.

programme.title: Piggy Builders
programme.desc: The neighbours give the Piggies impossible tasks to cover up a surprise party, but nothing is impossible for the Piggy Builders! Can the neighbours keep the party a secret?

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s Parsnip performing a jaw-dropping escape that would leave even Houdini speechless.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo and Bo need Ted’s help to pull a wobbly duck statue up Swoppiton Hill. But does Ted know the best way? And will there be anything left of the duck when they get there?

programme.title: Chuggington
programme.desc: Wilson is excited about being the new voice of Radio Chuggington, but when the chuggers decide to see a movie over listening to his radio stories, he exaggerates a news story that causes the town to panic!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: In Part 2, Supertato tells his side of the story. Yes, he did freeze everyone - but with Carrot's help, he realises that Evil Pea had tricked him, and he vows to make it right. Carrot helps Supertato master his powers - except his speed, which he still can’t control - and in his superhero costume, he’s ready to face Evil Pea. But she freezes him into a block of ice! He can’t break free until Carrot encourages him to use his potato speed. Soon, he bursts out of the ice block and speeds around melting the rest of the ice! It’s the first time Supertato saves the supermarket.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Coco discovers Bing's dressing-up box so they both dress up. Coco is Princess Cococapono and Bing is, of course, King Bing. But there is only one crown and both need it to complete their outfits. When the crown gets broken, Flop helps them to make new crowns out of the broken pieces.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Sula are building a stone tower in the Howly Woods when Sula finds an ammonite. Bing wants to find one too but is overwhelmed by the amount of stones, which makes it very difficult to find one. A frustrated Bing sits down, and Sula notices some ammonites in the rock behind him. Flop takes a picture of Bing and Sula with their ammonites.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee is blowing up balloons for Tino the artistic mouse's birthday. The Squirrels are a little worried because Tino can be a bit grumpy! But Duggee persuades them all to go and see Tino and give him a bunch of balloons. When you give a tiny mouse a big bunch of balloons, something unexpected happens. Tino starts to float up into the sky! He's having a rather good time, until he gets stuck in a tree. It's time for the Squirrels to come to his rescue.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee and the Squirrels decide to play hide-and-seek. Duggee counts to ten while the Squirrels go off and hide. They have hidden in really good places, but Duggee finds them all - except Roly. He's not in the tent. He's not in the clubhouse. He doesn't seem to be anywhere outside. Where could he be? Maybe the cows have seen where Roly is hiding.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Glitch creates big trouble with a little pyramid when he and the Go Jetters visit Egypt.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter realises he has accidentally upset Benjamin by asking him to sit out the next garden raid, he goes to apologise, only to find his cousin has gone.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: The Octonauts roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. Whether it is a perilous voyage to the bottom of the sea or the piratey pursuit of a giant squid, the Octonauts leap into action and always prove that eight heads are better than one! Captain Barnacles and crew must catch a runaway Octopod when it is hijacked by a group of crustaceans trying to escape their algae-infested waters.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: What top would be best for delivering parcels around town? Mojo and Bo need to decide fast and get those parcels delivered, whether it’s by land, water, or high in the air!

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Evie B wants to complete the Fantastic Bucket Challenge, but she doesn't think her attempts are good enough. The team offers to help, but she wants to do it herself. Will she succeed?

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friend pretend to be superheroes for the day. Meanwhile, Super Tumble goes to the rescue of Shopkeeper Tumble, Baker Tumble and Aunt Polly.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey's playgroup is at odds when Indy's baby hospital collides with Rusty's knights and dragons. But in explaining themselves, they both find that their games actually have a lot in common.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Dad agrees to take Bluey and Bingo to buy an ice cream if they can get him into the car.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Join Duggee, a big, lovable dog, as he runs the Squirrel Club, where children can earn badges for learning new skills. Warm-hearted preschool series about trying new things.

programme.desc: One is off on a camping adventure, but it can be lonely being the only one. Luckily, Two joins her just in time for a picnic. One puts a picnic blanket down, which is split into two equal parts - one part for One and one part for Two. When they get to the camp ground, they are joined by Three and Four, and together they discover how to split the camping space and baguette into equal parts.

programme.title: Colourblocks
programme.desc: Black joins the Printing Crew. Learn how yellow, cyan, magenta and black work together in printing with the Colourblocks.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: The Froglets don homemade skis and snowboards to whiz down a mountain of winter duvets.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Bella and Lift have fun playing with sponges, and so does Tincy the Spider in the Sing Song Forest - just watch out for those soapy bubbles!

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: A samba band is coming to play, and everyone is helping to prepare. Stripes is so busy that he has forgotten one thing - to book the band! With no band coming, all seems lost, until Yukee and Stripes realise the Sunhouse already has its own brilliant band!

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children use nets to catch toy fish in a water tray, learning BSL signs for fish, why and bit, then they sing and sign One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Once I Caught a Fish Alive.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Nick is looking at family photographs and creates a Popcast song about being a brother.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: The Piris plan a trip to Tippety Top to see the famous southern lights but lose each other in an ice fog. When Nugget thinks she sees a monster, Pancake proves to be an unlikely hero.

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: With Pearl entranced by Fifi’s glowing tummy mushrooms, Zog fears the worst when Gadabout attempts to mend Boom's wing himself.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants to blow a bubble just like her dads, but no matter how hard she tries, it won’t work. She makes a wish and creates a huge, magical bubble that floats around the park. As Rafi chases after it, the bubble spreads wonder wherever it goes. But when the bubble finally pops, Rafi is heartbroken. With help from her dads and friends, Rafi realises that bubbles aren’t meant to last forever, and that some of the most special moments are wonderful because they are fleeting.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo must prove Mr Monkeyjocks is special to save him from being chucked out.

programme.title: Nikhil & Jay
programme.desc: Nikhil and Jay start their own rock band. However, Nikhil feels deflated when Jay keeps inviting other people to join the band. Nikhil wants it to be just the two of them.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Umbrella is nervous about meeting up with his pen pal at the Parasol Show, so Sarah and Duck accompany him.

programme.title: Charlie and Lola
programme.desc: Children's animation. Join Lola and Charlie, a brother and sister, as they learn about growing up. When Charlie and Lola visit Granny and Grandpa, they always build an extremely special sandcastle on the beach, and they always do it together. This time a little girl and her family are determined to join in, and Lola's not too happy about it.

programme.title: Moon and Me
programme.desc: The discovery of a nursery rhyme book in the Toy House inspires Mr Onion to play at being Humpty Dumpty. When Humpty Onion refuses to fall off the wall, all the Toy House friends join in a game to make a comical new ending to the Humpty rhyme.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo plays with a block which is red like MeMo, and BaBa plays with a block that is yellow like BaBa. The friends continue across Planet BeddyByes and see more examples of their special colours: a yellow Tweetie, red and yellow Yummies, and a yellow omelette with red tomatoes. On the Lullaby Lake, reds and yellows mix in the setting sun to create a new, special colour.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read bedtime stories. Upsy Daisy wants to rest in her bed but is disturbed by one character after another. Finally, Upsy Daisy is left alone but discovers that she would much rather play with her friends after all.

programme.desc: Vicky McClure reads a Bedtime Story about a tiger on the hunt for his lost smile.
